issues.description: Constructor parameter order for ExcellenceLand in the solution does not follow the ordering required by the problem statement. The UML (and the task text) define ExcellenceLand attributes with excellencyLevel (double) first and excellentEnough (boolean) second, and the task additionally requires a private List<Ride> rides attribute. The solution's constructor is declared as ExcellenceLand(List<Ride> rides, boolean excellentEnough, double excellencyLevel) (rides first, then excellentEnough, then excellencyLevel), which contradicts the instruction that constructor parameters must appear in the same order as the UML (and, by reasonable extension, include the rides attribute in that order). This will confuse students implementing the required constructors and cause mismatch with automated tests that expect the specified parameter order.
issues.suggested_fix: Adjust the ExcellenceLand constructor in the solution to accept parameters in the order specified by the problem statement / UML. For example, declare the constructor as: public ExcellenceLand(double excellencyLevel, boolean excellentEnough, List<Ride> rides) and assign the fields accordingly (this.excellencyLevel = excellencyLevel; this.excellentEnough = excellentEnough; this.rides = rides;). Alternatively, if the intended parameter order is different, update the problem statement to explicitly state the constructor parameter order to match the solution.
